allChecks: Systems nominal. Your design passes the initial checks.
educational: Educational simulation · not for real engineering
intro: Space begins at your design desk. Build a spacecraft, balance its resources and take your mission beyond Earth.
featuredDesc: Six objectives. Eight orbits. A spacecraft designed by you.
footerNote: Made to explore, learn and work together.
stepDescriptions: Define the purpose of your mission.
Choose where you will observe the universe.
Give your spacecraft power, memory and control.
Find the path to your destination.
Make sure everything is ready to fly.
scenarioChange: Changing scenario loads a compatible starting design.
orbitDesc: Altitude, eclipses and contact windows shape power, data and coverage.
payloadDesc: More instruments generate more science, but also consume mass, power and bandwidth.
subsystemsDesc: Choose one option per subsystem. Combine solar panels and an RTG, or leave either power source out.
groundDesc: More contacts let you download more data, at a higher operations cost.
launcherDesc: Payload capacity depends on destination. A powerful launcher may still be unable to reach your selected orbit.
reviewDesc: Your PDR/CDR review. Check margins, resolve warnings and commit your design to launch.
seedHelp: Same design + same seed = same events. Share it for a fair competition.
launchWarning: Critical issues remain. You can simulate to learn from the consequences.
massTip: Total spacecraft mass versus launcher capacity to this destination. Adding instruments needs more launch capacity.
powerTip: Average generation after eclipses versus operational consumption. Batteries keep the spacecraft running in shadow.
budgetTip: Development + launch + operations, in millions of dollars. In-flight contingencies may increase the cost.
dataTip: Daily data produced versus download capacity: link speed × contact minutes. The excess fills storage.
storageTip: Estimated free memory after accumulating data that cannot be downloaded during the mission.
timeTip: Development months and operational duration. A longer mission produces more science and costs more.
orbitVisual: Artistic orbital visualization; distances not to scale
